The academic system is as follows: 6.1 The Institute operates a bi-semester academic system. The academic year is divided into two regular semesters: the first semester and the second semester, and there may be a special semester. One regular semester consists of not less than 15 weeks on instruction and the special semester may be arranged as required by each academic division and with the number of class periods and credits equaling those of a regular semester. “ree 6.2 The Institute may also operate other educational systems, such as tri-semester system, module (group of courses) system, distance education, and others, provided that the period of study and the number of credits are in proportion to those of the bi-semester system. 6.3 Each program offered by the Institute consists of a number of courses. Each course organizes the content based on the number of credits. The number of credits granted for each course is determined as follows: 6.3.1 A theory-based course entailing at least 15 hours of lectures or discussion or instruction per one regular semester shall be measured as one credit in the bi-semester academic system. 6.3.2 A practice-based course entailing at least 30 hours of training or laboratory sessions per one regular semester shall be measured as one credit in the bi-semester academic system. 6.3.3 The number of credits of a course involving both theoretical and practical sessions will be measured in accordance with the criteria stipulated under 6.3.1 and 6.3.2. 6.3.4 Apprenticeship, fieldwork practice or other training entailing at least 45 hours per one regular semester shall be measured as one credit in the bi-semester academic system. However, it may be established that credit is not counted for such course.

Gap khao means that you order a couple of dishes that come on full plates, and you order a plate of rice apart. text: [Article 8. Educational management system is as follows:] 8.1 The Institute operates a bi-semester academic system. Each academic year is divided into two regular semesters: first and second semesters. There may also be a special semester. Each regular semester consists of not less than 15 weeks and can also be divided into certain phases. A special semester can be organized according to the necessity of each program and the length of time and number of credits shall be determined in proportion to those in the regular semester. 8.2 The Institute may also operate other educational systems, such as trisemester system, module (group of courses) system, distance education, and others, provided that the period of study and the number of credits are in proportion to those of the bi-semester system. 8.3. Each undergraduate program offered at the Institute consists of multiple courses. Each course organizes the content based on the number of credits. The number of credits granted for each course is determined as follows: 8.3.1 A theory-based course involving lectures or discussion or instruction of not less than 15 hours per one regular semester shall be measured as one credit in the bi-semester system. 8.3.2 A practice-based course involving training or laboratory session of a minimum of 30 hours per one regular semester shall be measured as one credit in the bi-semester system. 8.3.3 The number of credits of a course involving both theoretical and practical sessions will be measured in accordance with the criteria stipulated under 8.3.1 and 8.3.2. 8.3.4 Training practice, field study, or any other training that takes not less than 45 hours per a regular semester shall be measured as one credit in the bi-semester system.

text: [Article 6. The academic system is as follows: The bi-semester academic year is divided into] 6.1 The Institute operates a bi-semester academic system. text: Article 24. Grade Point Average Calculation 24.1 Grade point average will be calculated at the end of each semes ter. To calculate the grade point avera ge, multiply the number of credi ts with the grade received and, then, divide the total number of cred its registered in for the semest er concerned. The final accumulated grade point average may carry only 2 decimal points. Re-registered co urses under Article 11 shall be included in the calculation of grade point average, but not those courses that yield the results of S, U or T. 24.2 Three types of grade point average shall be calculated: 24.2.1 Grade Point Average of Semester (GPS) is calculated from all courses registered in the semester concerned; 24.2.2 Cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) is calculated from every course taken from the first semester to the current one; and 24.2.3 Grade point average based on program structure means the grade point average calculated from only the courses required by the program. Undergraduate Honors] 29.2.1 First Class Honors and Gold Medal: the student must obtain the highest cumulative GPA based on the program structure among the group of graduates in the same academic year in each program. Article 34. Leave 34.1 There are four categories of leave as follows: 34.1.1 Sick leave; 34.1.2 Personal business leave; 34.1.3 leave of absence; and 34.1.4 Resignation. 34.2 Sick leave 34.2.1 If a sick leave is taken during instruction, students must subm it a sick leave application form on the first day of return. If sick leav e is taken for five days or more, a medical certificate must be produced to the course lecturers. 34.2.2 If a sick leave is taken during examination, requirements of paragraph 22.3.1 shall be observed. 34.3 Personal business leave 34.3.1 If students have to take a personal business leave during a cla ss, they need to obtain permission of the course lecturer. 34.3.2 Students who need to take a personal business leave for one day or more must file a leave application form, which must contain the reason for leave and representation of either the students’ custodian or advisor, to the course lecturer before the leave date. 34.3.3 To take a personal business leave during examination, students have to comply with requirements of 22.3.2-22.3.3 and 22.4. 34.4 Leave of absence 34.4.1 A leave of absence refers to a leave taken for an entire semest er. If a student has registered for courses, such registration shall be considered to have been terminated and all registered courses will not appear in the transcript.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: [Article 34. Leave] 34.4.2 Leave of absence will be permitted in the following cases: 34.4.2.1 Illness with medical certificate issued by public or private hospital indicating that the student is in need for recovery; 34.4.2.2 Accident, which requires more than 20 days of recovery; 34.4.2.3 Military recruitment or mobilization; 34.4.2.4 Being awarded an international scholarship or other that the Institute deems appropraite to support; or -14- 34.4.2.5 Failure to register for coures or make payment of tuition fee within the time designated by the Institute. 34.4.3 The student may apply for a leave of absence for one regular semester at a time and the leave cannot be taken consecutively for over one academic year. The student or his/her custodian in the case where the student is unable to be present on his/her own, shall submit a petition for leave of absence as well as evid ence, as the case may be, to th e Office of the Registrar. Application for leave of absence must have the consent of the student’s custodi an and be completed before the final examination of the semester that the student wishes to take a leave of absence. 34.4.4 New students are not entitled to request for leave of absence i n the first semester, except in case of a force majeure where the Pre sident will consider approving the request on a case-by-case basis. 34.4.5 The student whose request for leave of absence is approved must make payment of fee to maintain his/her student status in every regular semester, except the semester in which in the student has already registered for courses and paid the tuition fee.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: [Article 34. Leave] 34.4.6 The student who wishes to take a leave of absence for more than one academic year must gain approval of the Director of the Office of the Registrar and pay a fee to maintain his/her student status every regular semester. 34.4.7 The period of the absence must be computed as part of the duration of study in the program. 34.5 In order to resign, the student must submit a petition for resi gnation together with consent of the student’s custodian to the Director of the Office of the Registrar. No approval will be granted if the student has financial obligations due to the Institute. 34.6 Student status will be terminated in the following circumstances: 34.6.1 Death; 34.6.2 Resignation; 34.6.3 Penalty of dismissal under Chapter 13; 34.6.4 Lack of qualifications of a student of the Institute; 34.6.5 Failure to register for coures; 34.6.6 Failure to maintain student sta tus witin the time designated by t h e Institute; 34.6.7 The maximum period of study under 6.4 is exceeded, provided tha t the period of leave of absence or penalty suspension is computed as a part of the period of study; or 34.6.8 Cheating in an exam for more than once. 34.6.9 The Institute issues an announcement declaring that the student i s terminated due to violation of the regulations or rules of the Institute; and 34.6.10 Failure to make payment of the tuition fee and fine under 10.5. 34.7 At the end of every semester, the Office of the Registrar must announce the names of students who are terminated and remove them from the s tudent register, provided that consent is granted by the head of academic division.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: [Article 34. Leave] 34.8 In the case where a student’ status as the Institute student is terminated due to decease, the accepting academic division must inform related units as soon as possible. -15- 34.9 In case of necessity, the student who was terminated due to “re signation” under 34.5 or failure to register and maintain his/her student status may file an application for return to the Institute. Such application must be approved by the Preside nt with consent of the head of academic division that the student belongs to. In this regard, the student is required to apply for retrospective leave of absence and make payment of all tuition fees. The applicatio n must be made no later than one year from the date of termination and not contrary to the period of study requirement under 6.4. Chapter 12 Special Semester ………………. Article 35. The student of the Institute who is to register for a course in a special semester must file a petition with the head of academic division that is responsible for that course to offer the course.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: Article 36. The course to be offered in the summer semester mus t be a course available in the program of each academic division. The head of academic divisio n will approve the offering of the course when a lecturer who is able to teach that course is available to teach. In the case where there is no lecturer available to teach the c ourse, the student may choose to take a course offered by anothe r program with equivalent conten t with the course that the student wants to take by filing a petition for course equivalency recognition with the head of the academic division for approval before registering for that course. After that, the academic division must notify the Office of the Registrar for further action. Article 37. The special semester is made up of not less than fi ve weeks of instruction with the number of class periods for each course equaling those of a regular semester. Article 38. Registration for courses in a special semester shal l be as provided in the second paragraph of Article 10.4. Article 39. Addition or change of courses must be completed wit hin one week from the start of the semester. Course withdrawal must be done one week before th e start of the special semester, unless there is a force majeure under 22.3. Article 40. Evaluation and gradi ng shall be as per requirements of Chapter 8. Article 41. Payment of tuition fee shall be as stipulated in th e Institute’s related regulations or announcements. Chapter 13 Student’s Discipline ………………. Article 42. Students must strictly conform to the discipline he reunder at all times. Failure to comply with the following shall be regarded as violation of dis cipline and punishment shall be imposed as defined in these regulations.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: [Article 42. Students must strictly conform to the discipline he reunder at all times. Failure] 42.1 Students must dress appropriately. 42.2 Students must show respect to lecturers and staff of the Institute. 42.3 Students must behave in an appropriate manner and must not cons titute any disgrace to themselves or the Institute. -16- 42.4 Students must not smoke during instruction or examination or in the Institute. 42.5 Students must not drink liquors or consume intoxicants in the Institute. 42.6 The following acts are considered serious disciplinary offenses: 42.6.1 Slander that causes others to suffer damages as well as instiga ting, supporting or leading any chaotic event within the Institute’s premises, such as fight, destruction of property of the Institute or govern mental agency, delinquent ac ts, and demonstration consisting of more than 10 persons in violation of laws; 42.6.2 Consumption of liquors or intoxicants in the Institute; 42.6.3 Using illegal or narcotic drugs; 42.6.4 Carrying weapons or illegal articles; 42.6.5 Cheating in exams; 42.6.6 Displaying any behavior that is disrespectful to lecturers or s taff members of the Institute who carry out duties in accordance wit h laws or the Institute’s regulations or rules, which is deemed a serious disciplinary offense by the Discipline Committee; 42.6.7 Forging the signature of custodian or another person and using it as evidence when contacting the Institute, which causes damages to the Institute; 42.6.8 Engaging in any type of gambling in the Institute; 42.6.9 Carrying out any act that damages or defames the Institute, suc h as being hired to take exam for other person, either in or outside the Institute, copying other person’s thesis or academic paper, or hiring any person to write a thesis or academic paper; and 42.6.10 Carrying out any other act that is deemed a serious offense by the Discipline Committee and the President.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: Article 43. There are three modest disciplinary actions as foll ows: 43.1 Verbal warning; 43.2 Probation; and 43.3 Compensation for damage caused. Article 44. There are three serious disciplinary actions as fol lows: 44.1. Suspension of study; 44.2. Expulsion; and 44.3. Dismissal. Article 45. If the student commits any disciplinary offenses un der Article 42, except for 42.6.5, the President may order a penalty proportional to the offense c ommitted. However, if there is any reason for mitigation of the penalty, such reason may be taken into consideration. -17- Article 46. In the case where a student cheats in exam under 42 .6.5 and there is clear evidence of such cheat, the head of academic division must conduct and c omplete an investigation of the student’s offense as soon as possible from the date of detection and prop ose the investigation result to the President to impose a penalty under Article 23. After the Presi dent has issued and signed a penalty order, the academic division must notify the student of such penalty order without delay as well as the Office of the Registrar.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: Article 47. In the case where any student is accused of committ ing any disciplinary offense under Article 42, except for cheating in exam under 42.6.5, the Discipline Committee appointed by the Institute shall have the power t o initiate a disciplinary actio n against the accused student immediately to investigate the offense in a fair and quick manner. The penalty in proportion to severity of the offense committed must then be proposed to the President for approval. After the President has issued a penalty order, the Discipline Committee must notify the student of such penalty order without delay. The head of academic division the student belongs to and the Office of the Registrar must also be notified. Appointment, assignment of power and duties, and meeting of the Discipline Committee shall be made in the form of the Institute’s announcement. Article 48. Any student on whom a penalty is imposed in accorda nce with Article 46 or Article 47 shall have the right to file a n appeal against the penalty w ith the President within 30 days from the date of receipt of the penalty order. The appeal must be made in writing and signed by the appellant. After the President has considered the appeal, the Discipline C ommittee appointed by the Institute or the head of academic division, as the case may be, shall proceed in accordance with the he President’s order without delay. Chapter 14 Dignity and Honor of Students to Receive the Degree or Diploma ………………. Article 49. Students who are eligible to be nominated for a deg ree or diploma must possess all qualifications under Article 27.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: Article 50. Students who are suitable for being nominated to th e Institute Council to receive the Institute’s degree or diploma shall not only have dignity, hono r and morality, maintain good reputation, prestige and benefits of the Institute, comply with the student’s discipline and regulations of the Institute, but also need to have the following qualifications: 50.1 Not being diagnosed as a person of unsound mind by a medical do ctor or adjudged as incompetent or quasi-incompetent by the court; 50.2 Not being imprisoned pursuant to a final judgment or undergoing c r i m i n a l prosecution, except for offenses arising out of negligence or for petty offenses; 50.3 Not being a person of evil, immoral or roguish behavior, consum ing alcoholic beverage to the point of being unable to maintain a sound mind, being insolvent, being immersed oneself in gambling, or engaging in improper sexual relationship, which constitute disgrace to the Institute; 50.4 Not causing disunity or fight among fellow students or between the Institute’s students and those of another institution or other persons; -18- 50.5 Not displaying any behavior disrespectful or insulting towards the Institute’s lectures or personnel who carry out duties in accordance with laws or the Institute’s regulations or rules; 50.6 Not interfering with the power to administer the Institute; 50.7 Not intentionally causing serious damage to the Institute’s property; 50.8 Not copying or hiring another person to write a thesis, special problem, or similar course called by another name, for oneself 50.9 Not being hired to write a thesis, special problem, or similar course called by another name, for another person, or being hired to take exam for another person; 50.10 Not copying the thesis of oneself or another person; and 50.11 Not having any financial obligations due to the Institute.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: Article 51. To apply for approval to receive the degree, studen ts must comply with and adhere to all requirements and procedures as well as date, time and pl ace indicated in the Institute’s academic calendar, and pay the fee to receive the certificate or degree as required by the Institute. Article 52. The student who lack s any qualifications under Arti cle 50 will be regarded as lacking dignity and honor and not being eligible for the degree . Any one of the following decision may be made with respect to such student: 52.1 The student will not be nominated for receiving the Institute’s degree; or 52.2 Nomination for the degree will be delayed for one to three acad emic years in proportion to severity of the offense committed; or 52.3 Revocation of degree: in the case where the Institute has found that a graduate for whom the Institute Council h as approved the degree is not q ualified under Article 50, the Institute Council shall consider revoking th e degree. The revocation will be effective form the date the Institute Council approves to confer the degree on such person.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: Article 53. At the end of each academic year, if there are any students lacking the qualifications under Article 50, the Academic Division Committee shall proceed in accordance with Article 52 and send the consideration result to the Office of the Registrar, w hich will further propose the result to the Institute Council for approval. In case of a student who is con sidered by the Institute Council as unsuitable for receiving the degree, if he/she deems that he/sh e is treated unfairly, the student has the right to file a written appeal bearing his/her signature with t he President. A certified copy of the appeal must also be submitted to the head of academic division within 15 working days from the date the student is aware that he/she is considered unsuitable for receiving the degree. Article 54. The head of academic division must submit a clarifi cation of the appeal to the Institute within seven working days from the date of receipt of the certified copy of such appeal under Article 53. Article 55. When the President receives the appeal together wit h the clarification given by the head of academic division, they must be presented to the meetin g of the executive board of the institute for consideration as soon as possible. The result will then be proposed to the Institute Council for the final decision. Article 56. In the case where the student is not satisfied with the decision regarding the appeal under Article 55, he/she may submit a request for reconsideration of the appeal in the following cases:

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: [Article 56. In the case where the student is not satisfied with the decision regarding] 56.1 There is new evidence, which may significantly change the accou nt of the matter; or -19- 56.2 The decision on the prior appeal was made on the basis of any i nformation or provision of law, which has later changed significantly in a way that is beneficial to the student. Submission of the request under the first paragraph can be made only if the student was not aware of that circumstance before in the previous consi deration, provided that such unawareness was not the student’s fault. Submission of the request under the first paragraph must be mad e within 30 days from the date the student is aware of the circumstance that ena bles him/her to make a request for reconsideration. Chapter 15 Miscellaneous ………………. Article 57. Exam answer sheets must be kept by the academic division for at least one academic year from the date of announcement of the examination results. At the end of such period, the head of academic division shall have the power to order a destruction of these documents. Article 58. The Office of the Registrar must keep the score rep orts of each course for a minimum of five years from the date of announcement of the exam ination results. After the end of such period, the Director of the Office of the Registrar shall have the power to order a destruction of these documents. Chapter 16 Transitory Provisions ………………. Article 59. In case of doubt regarding application of these reg ulations, the President shall issue orders as he/she may deem fit for a particular matter on a case -by-case basis. If such matter is related to students enrolling before these regulations come into effect, t he President must also take the earlier regulations, rules or criteria into consideration when making a decision.

title: KMITL Undergraduate Regulations 2016
text: Article 60. During the period of no rules, notifications, order s, or resolutions being issued under these regulations, those rules, notifications, orders, or resol utions in force on the date these regulations come into force shall apply, mutatis mutandis, as far as they are not contrary to these regulations until there are rules, notifications, orders or resolutions issued for the application of these regulations.
